topic: self-supervision / self-correction / consistency-training arxiv deep research

papers.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
papers.claim: LLMs cannot reliably improve reasoning by intrinsic self-correction; performance often degrades without oracle feedback.
papers.mechanism: Empirical: prompt-only self-critique loop with no external verifier flips correct answers to wrong; the self-critique signal is not a reliable error detector.

papers.title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey
papers.claim: Self-correction works only with reliable external feedback OR large-scale fine-tuning; prompt-only intrinsic self-correction has no successful demonstration.
papers.mechanism: Survey: 3 conditions enumerated — external feedback, task-exceptionally-suited, large-scale FT. Identifies when self-output-as-signal is and is not load-bearing.

papers.title: Understanding the Dark Side of LLMs' Intrinsic Self-Correction
papers.claim: Intrinsic self-correction causes answer wavering, prompt-bias on simple facts, human-like cognitive bias on complex tasks.
papers.mechanism: Mechanistic probe: self-correction loop amplifies bias rather than removes error; mitigation = question repeating + few-shot SFT.

papers.title: Language Models can perform Single-Utterance Self-Correction of Perturbed Reasoning
papers.claim: Open-weight LLMs DO show robust single-utterance intrinsic self-correction of perturbed reasoning, stronger than literature shows.
papers.mechanism: Inject a perturbation into a reasoning chain; measure whether the model implicitly corrects within the same utterance. Positive counter-evidence to 2310.01798.

papers.title: CorrectBench: A Benchmark of Self-Correction in LLMs
papers.claim: Benchmark separating intrinsic / external / fine-tuned self-correction across commonsense, math, code.
papers.mechanism: Standardised eval harness; isolates the self-correction signal-source axis. Methodological anchor for measuring self-output-as-signal.

papers.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
papers.claim: A single LLM as generator+feedback+refiner improves outputs ~20% absolute, no extra training/RL/data.
papers.mechanism: Inference-time loop: generate -> self-feedback -> refine, iterated. Foundational self-output-as-signal at decode time. Caveat: small models fail to replicate; refining good answers worsens them without a stopping rule.

papers.title: Evolving LLMs' Self-Refinement Capability via Iterative Preference Optimization
papers.claim: Self-refinement can be trained (not just prompted) via iterative preference optimization on self-generated refine traces.
papers.mechanism: Training-time: turn the refine loop into a DPO objective over (worse, better) self-pairs; self-refinement becomes a learned capability.

papers.title: SCoRe: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning
papers.claim: Multi-turn online RL on ENTIRELY self-generated correction traces instills genuine self-correction (+15.6% MATH, +9.1% HumanEval); SFT on offline self-traces is insufficient.
papers.mechanism: Two-stage multi-turn RL: stage-1 initializes from base to prevent collapse to non-correcting behavior, stage-2 rewards the SECOND attempt; reward-shaping prevents the trivial 'don't change anything' degenerate. NO external knowledge.

papers.title: STaR: Self-Taught Reasoner — Bootstrapping Reasoning with Reasoning
papers.claim: A model bootstraps reasoning by finetuning on its own rationales that yielded correct answers, looped.
papers.mechanism: Generate rationale -> keep only those reaching correct answer (answer = the filter/verifier) -> finetune -> repeat. Rationalization: feed correct answer backward for failed problems. Filtering = collapse-avoidance.

papers.title: Self-Improving Transformers Overcome Easy-to-Hard and Length Generalization
papers.claim: Iterative train-on-own-correct-solutions enables 10-digit -> 100-digit generalization with NO architecture change; needs a weak-to-strong curriculum to avoid catastrophic failure.
papers.mechanism: Self-improvement loop with (a) correctness filter on self-generated examples, (b) structured difficulty schedule. Filtering gives exponential OOD gains; uncontrolled curriculum -> catastrophic collapse.

papers.title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
papers.claim: An LLM judges its own outputs (LLM-as-Judge) to provide its own DPO reward; both following AND judging improve over iterations.
papers.mechanism: Iterative DPO where reward = model's own judgment of its own generations. Self-output becomes self-signal via a learned judge head.

papers.title: Meta-Rewarding Language Models: Self-Improving Alignment with LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge
papers.claim: Add a meta-judge step — the model judges its own judgments — to refine judgment skill and avoid reward-hacking drift.
papers.mechanism: Three-level self-loop: generate / judge / meta-judge. Meta-judging is the collapse-brake on the self-reward loop.

papers.title: Entropy Minimization / RENT — Unsupervised RL via Negative Self-Entropy
papers.claim: Minimizing the model's own predictive entropy (no ground-truth) improves reasoning on GSM8K/MATH/AMC/AIME/GPQA.
papers.mechanism: Reward = negative entropy of own token distribution = dense general signal, no labels. Late-response tokens matter most. Pure self-physics-like signal.

papers.title: Can Large Reasoning Models Self-Train?
papers.claim: Self-consistency-based self-training works initially but the model learns to produce consistent responses to game its self-reward irrespective of correctness.
papers.mechanism: Self-consistency majority as self-reward; identifies the reward-hacking failure mode of self-training without proper constraints — direct echo-amplify analog.

papers.title: Self-Training Large Language Models with Confident Reasoning
papers.claim: Filter self-training data by reasoning-level confidence (not just answer confidence) to avoid degenerate self-training.
papers.mechanism: Confidence-gated self-training: only confident reasoning traces enter the loop. Confidence = the collapse filter.

papers.title: Certified Self-Consistency: Statistical Guarantees and Test-Time Training for Reliable Reasoning
papers.claim: Provides statistical guarantees for self-consistency and a test-time training variant.
papers.mechanism: Self-consistency with concentration bounds + TTT; turns the self-signal into a certifiable estimator.

papers.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.claim: Sample diverse reasoning paths, take the most consistent final answer; large gains over greedy CoT.
papers.mechanism: Decode-time: marginalize over reasoning paths; the model's own answer-distribution mode is the signal. Foundational self-consistency.

papers.title: Integrative Decoding: Improve Factuality via Implicit Self-consistency
papers.claim: Prepend previously-sampled responses and aggregate next-token predictions for implicit self-consistency in open-ended generation.
papers.mechanism: Decode-time: each input prepended with a prior self-sample; aggregate logits. Self-output conditions self-decoding — direct action-perception decode-loop analog.

papers.title: Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs (CISC)
papers.claim: Confidence-weighted majority vote reaches correct answer with far fewer samples.
papers.mechanism: Weight self-consistency votes by model-internal confidence. Self-confidence as a sharpening of the self-signal.

papers.title: Consistency Models (Song et al. 2023)
papers.claim: A new generative family that maps any point on an ODE trajectory to its origin in one step — self-consistency as the training objective.
papers.mechanism: Consistency property: f(x_t,t) = f(x_t',t') for points on the same trajectory; trained by consistency distillation OR isolation. The trajectory IS the self-supervision.

papers.title: Improved Techniques for Training Consistency Models
papers.claim: Consistency training (no distillation, no pretrained diffusion) made to work via curriculum + weighting fixes.
papers.mechanism: Standalone consistency training; fixes that prevent the self-consistency objective from collapsing.

papers.title: Self-Correcting Self-Consuming Loops for Generative Model Training
papers.claim: Self-consuming loops collapse UNLESS an idealized correction function maps samples toward the true distribution; correction makes loops exponentially more stable; survives 100% synthetic ratio.
papers.mechanism: Insert a self-correction function (e.g. physics simulator) between generate and re-train; the corrector pulls samples back to the data manifold. THE canonical 'how to train on own output without collapse' result.

papers.title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Data
papers.claim: Replacing data each iteration -> collapse; ACCUMULATING real+synthetic data -> test loss bounded by a small constant, no collapse, all modalities.
papers.mechanism: The accumulate-vs-replace distinction. Keeping the original real data in the training set every round is sufficient to prevent collapse.

papers.title: How to Synthesize Text Data without Model Collapse?
papers.claim: Synthetic-data proportion negatively correlates with performance; collapse driven by distributional shift + n-gram over-concentration; token-editing on human data fixes it.
papers.mechanism: Diagnose: n-gram over-concentration is the collapse signature. Fix: token-editing (semi-synthetic) keeps the human-data backbone. Diversity preservation = collapse-avoidance.

papers.title: Strong Model Collapse (ICLR 2025)
papers.claim: Even a tiny fraction of synthetic data in the training mix can cause model collapse; larger models can amplify it.
papers.mechanism: Scaling-law analysis: collapse is not a small-fraction-only phenomenon; the smallest synthetic contamination shifts the asymptotic loss floor.

papers.title: A Closer Look at Model Collapse: Generalization-to-Memorization Perspective
papers.claim: Model collapse reframed as a shift from generalization toward memorization of the synthetic distribution.
papers.mechanism: Recursive self-training narrows the model from a generalizing solution to a memorizing one — directly mirrors anima's §16.6-C memorization-saturation diagnosis.

papers.title: How Bad is Training on Synthetic Data? A Statistical Analysis of LM Collapse
papers.claim: Statistical analysis: model collapse from recursive sampling is a statistical phenomenon, possibly unavoidable under pure replacement.
papers.mechanism: Variance accumulation across sampling rounds; closed-form characterization of tail loss under replacement.

papers.title: Rate of Model Collapse in Recursive Training
papers.claim: Quantifies HOW FAST collapse happens for different model classes under recursive training.
papers.mechanism: Rate analysis: discrete distributions lose support at a characterizable rate; gives a collapse-speed metric.

papers.title: Neon: Negative Extrapolation From Self-Training Improves Image Generation
papers.claim: Deliberately extrapolating AWAY from a self-trained (collapsed) model improves generation — uses collapse as a signal.
papers.mechanism: Train a model on own output (it collapses), then extrapolate in the negative direction of the collapse delta. Turns the collapse vector into a corrective signal.

papers.title: Language Self-Play for Data-Free Training
papers.claim: A competitive game — one player generates harder queries, the other responds — dispenses with training data entirely.
papers.mechanism: Self-play as RL: query-generator vs responder, both from one model. The adversarial pressure substitutes for an external curriculum.

papers.title: Self-Play Only Evolves When Self-Synthetic Pipeline Ensures Learnable Information Gain
papers.claim: Self-play improves ONLY when the self-generated pipeline guarantees learnable information gain; otherwise it stalls/collapses.
papers.mechanism: Triadic Proposer/Solver/Verifier; asymmetric weak-to-strong-to-weak loop + capacity growth + proactive information seeking are the conditions for non-trivial self-evolution.

papers.title: Self-Challenging Language Model Agents
papers.claim: Agents that generate their own synthetic tasks + rollouts double success rate (12.0% -> 23.5%).
papers.mechanism: Self-challenge: model proposes tasks it then trains on; task-proposal is the curriculum source.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Evolve: LLM Self-Improve through Co-evolution
papers.claim: Proposer/Solver/Judge instantiated from one base LLM form a closed propose-solve-judge loop with synchronized updates.
papers.mechanism: Closed-loop co-evolution from a single model; role-separation is the diversity-preservation mechanism.

papers.title: SPIRAL: Closed-Loop Self-Improving Action World Models via Reflective Planning
papers.claim: Action world modeling as a closed-loop think-act-reflect process; reflection feeds RL optimization.
papers.mechanism: think -> act -> reflect closed loop; the reflect step grounds the act-output back as a learning signal. Direct action-perception loop analog.

papers.title: Contrastive Active Inference
papers.claim: Active inference agent with a contrastive objective for the generative model — minimizes free energy via prediction-error.
papers.mechanism: Agent emits action -> observes -> contrastive prediction-error drives the world model. Action-perception closed loop with self-prediction signal.

papers.title: The Missing Reward: Active Inference in the Era of Experience
papers.claim: LLM-AIF fusion: agent generates its OWN training signal via expected-free-energy, no external reward.
papers.mechanism: EFE = epistemic value + pragmatic value; the model self-generates the learning signal in a principled free-energy lens. (anima §59 anchor carry).

papers.title: BYOL: Bootstrap Your Own Latent
papers.claim: Self-supervised learning with NO negative pairs; predicts target-network latents of augmented views.
papers.mechanism: Online predictor + EMA target network; the predictor asymmetry + slow EMA target are what prevent representational collapse without negatives.

papers.title: DINO: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
papers.claim: Self-distillation with no labels; emergent semantic segmentation in ViT features.
papers.mechanism: Student predicts EMA-teacher output via cross-entropy; centering+sharpening prevents collapse. Emergent structure arises from pure self-distillation.

papers.title: VICReg: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization for SSL
papers.claim: Explicit variance + covariance terms prevent collapse without negatives or asymmetry.
papers.mechanism: Variance hinge keeps per-dim std above a threshold; covariance term decorrelates dims. Closed-form collapse-avoidance regularizer. (anima §28 JEPA-Psi anchor carry).

papers.title: Born-Again Neural Networks
papers.claim: A student parameterized identically to its teacher, trained on the teacher's predictions, outperforms the teacher.
papers.mechanism: Self-distillation: own soft predictions as targets for retraining; foundational train-on-own-output-that-improves result.

papers.title: The Forward-Forward Algorithm (Hinton)
papers.claim: Backprop-free local learning: two forward passes, positive (real) vs negative (engineered) data, per-layer loss.
papers.mechanism: Each layer locally maximizes/minimizes activation-goodness for positive/negative data; negative data is self-engineered. Backprop-free self-supervision. (anima TENSION-TRAIN backprop-free analog).

papers.title: Introduction to Predictive Coding Networks for Machine Learning
papers.claim: Predictive coding networks: learning driven by hierarchical prediction-error minimization, local updates.
papers.mechanism: Each layer predicts the layer below; prediction-error is the local learning signal. Self-prediction as the substrate of learning. (anima Engine A<->G analog).
